mark.does: The Māori chin marking worn by women.

text.what: The Māori chin marking worn by women.
text.story: Michael King interviewed more than seventy women in the 1970s who had received it before 1907. Since the 1990s it has been worn by a foreign minister and a prime-time news anchor, which is a change in where the mark is allowed to be seen rather than in the mark.
